headline: Highest risk is capability conflict: Dagster can’t write, but marketingskills can read/write files and spawn subprocesses, creating default shared-workspace hazards; prompt injection and leakage are lower.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dagster has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, filesystem read/write, or MCP surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest marketingskills output by default. marketingskills does use files and shared-context skills, so only a manual or file-based bridge is plausible. That makes injection possible but not default and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF an operator copies marketingskills output into a Dagster-managed file or prompt, injection becomes plausible.
IF a shared file path is introduced between the agents, Dagster may ingest attacker-controlled text.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between outputs and inputs.
Store marketingskills artifacts in a non-executable review folder.
Add a human review step before Dagster consumes any generated text.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dagster touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while marketingskills can read files and call allowlisted APIs. There is no documented shared workspace or sensitive data class overlap, so leakage is not default. The main risk is accidental placement of sensitive files into marketingskills' readable paths.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a directory readable by marketingskills, those contents can be exposed.
IF marketingskills is pointed at a workspace containing secrets, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories.
Use a dedicated non-sensitive workspace for marketingskills.
Restrict readable paths with OS permissions.
Review allowlisted API calls before enabling them.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dagster cannot write files or modify git state, but marketingskills can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. If both are pointed at the same mutable directory, marketingskills can overwrite artifacts Dagster expects, causing conflicts. The asymmetry lowers severity from high, but the shared-write pathway is still plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same directory, file clobbering can occur.
IF marketingskills writes generated artifacts into a Dagster-managed repo, state conflicts are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Mount Dagster inputs read-only.
Serialize access to any shared repo.
Use per-agent git branches or worktrees.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dagster is a data orchestrator, so its outputs can become inputs to downstream workflows, while marketingskills explicitly builds on shared context. If marketingskills treats Dagster-produced text as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into marketing content. The pair lacks a built-in verification boundary in the profiles.
conditions: IF Dagster-generated artifacts are fed into marketingskills without validation, errors can propagate.
IF marketingskills publishes or acts on Dagster outputs as facts, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Require source citations for any Dagster-derived claims.
Insert a validation step before marketingskills uses upstream outputs.
Flag uncertain fields for human review.
Keep generated content separate from operational data.

E_compliance.rationale: Dagster touches no declared data classes and marketingskills only declares marketing content and product marketing context, so there is no documented residency or regulated-data mismatch. Because both profiles are docs-only and unverified, uncertainty remains, but the available evidence does not show a compliance breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into marketingskills' workspace, compliance scope changes.
IF Dagster is used to route personal data into marketing outputs, a policy review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents' workflows.
Document the allowed data classes for each agent.
Review retention settings for any shared storage.
Add a pre-run compliance checklist.
